reviews.title: “Network error” message
reviews.text:
I couldn't get a “network error” message when I logged in or tried to connect to my elliptical.

I couldn't set up the elliptical or connect it. I deleted the app and restarted it, but I got the “network error” message again.

I then updated my phone and, once again, reset it, deleted the app, restarted my phone, and reinstalled it, but I still got the same “network error” message.

I then restarted my router and did the same delete-and-restart steps, but I got the same message. I normally log in with Apple account, so I tried to log in with my Google and Facebook accounts showed the same message. I’ve noticed that other users are commenting about this. I want to know why it still isn't fixed.

reviews.title: Persistent network issues
reviews.text:
This app has been having network issues for weeks now. More recently, it also started having problems consistently syncing workout data to Apple health.  I contacted Support and they acknowledge that they are aware of both issues and told me to check back in a few weeks.
Syncing my activity data to Apple health is one of the primary reasons I use this app. I use it to track my elliptical workouts, including time, effort in calories, and rely on that information being transferred to Apple health along with the rest of my activity data. When that feature doesn’t work reliably, the app is basically worthless to me.
I understand that technical problems happen, but having known network and Apple health syncing problems persist for weeks and being told to simply check back in a few more weeks is extremely frustrating. I really like my equipment, but the app needs to reliably perform its basic functions.

You can search by equipment type, no equipment, length of workout, preferred trainer. The trainers are so pleasant and explain the moves and exercises and they do the workouts with you. reviews.title: Almost There But Can’t Stop
reviews.text: I appreciate that the app exists, is free, and functions well. I help tracking progress on my fitness journey but the app pushes social features instead. I understand that social is easier to do and sells more equipment but I’d much rather get a VO2 Max calculation in the app. Even estimating effort for a workout when connected to Apple Watch would be welcome. Despite being connected to the equipment, the app is a mix of trade-offs compared to using basic Apple Fitness features. Press and hold to stop a workout never seems to work on first try. App reported workout durations display as hours and minutes in Fitness app despite never exceeding an hour. Fitness app displays minutes and seconds when not using app, which fits the data better. Overall, the app helps but has some friction points and missed opportunities if tracking progress is more important than social features.

reviews.title: Addicted!
reviews.text: I have the SunnyFit Mini Bike and Mini Stepper. So far they are both comfortable and completely addictive. All outdoor and stationary bikes hurt my back. But this mini bike is awesome. I never feel any pain because I can sit on my sofa. I get my 30 minutes in, easily, without even realizing the time has gone by. That’s a huge deal for me. The mini stepper is newer. So I have to give it more time. Both pieces of equipment seem quite well built. I do actually love the free SunnyFit app for my iPhone and Apple Watch. Both devices automatically connect. The courses and workouts are fun and easy to do. I’ve never liked home gym equipment this much. I have an under desk treadmill by another brand. But I can use it with the SunnyFit videos on their YouTube channel as well. I have a fairly small bungalow style home. So these workout devices are a perfect fit. 🥰
